Every analysis in the other articles is a method of the `IsoformicExperiment` object, and each has a table-based counterpart for data that does not fit in the object, for example results already joined in a spreadsheet or a single gene exported from another tool.
This article shows those counterparts on the tables of the [introduction](isoformic-introduction.html).

```{r}
#| message: false
library(isoformic)
library(dplyr)

extdata <- fs::path_package("isoformic", "extdata")
abundance <- read_parquet(fs::path(extdata, "pe_abundance.parquet"))
col_data <- read_parquet(fs::path(extdata, "pe_col_data.parquet"))
det <- read_parquet(fs::path(extdata, "pe_det.parquet"))
deg <- read_parquet(fs::path(extdata, "pe_deg.parquet"))
annot_dir <- prepare_isoformic_annotation(download_reference(version = "33", file_type = "gff"))
```

## Transcript-to-gene table

`make_tx_to_gene()` builds the transcript-to-gene table from an annotation directory, a GENCODE transcript FASTA or a GFF3 file.

```{r}
tx2gene <- make_tx_to_gene(annot_dir)
head(tx2gene)
```

## Differential expression tables

`join_DEG_DET()` builds the long table that `plot_log2fc()` consumes from gene-level and transcript-level results, and `is_deg_sig()` flags significance with the same cutoffs the object uses.

```{r}
de_long <- join_DEG_DET(
  deg_table = left_join(deg, distinct(tx2gene, gene_id, gene_name), by = "gene_id"),
  det_table = left_join(det, tx2gene, by = "transcript_id"),
  logfc_cut = 1,
  pval_cut = 0.05
)
head(de_long)
plot_log2fc(de_long, feature = "RBPJ")
```

## Expression profiles

`prepare_profile_data()` builds the table for `plot_tx_expr()` from the abundance table, the sample metadata and the transcript-to-gene table.

```{r}
profile <- prepare_profile_data(
  txi_transcript = abundance,
  sample_metadata = col_data,
  tx_to_gene = tx2gene,
  de_result_gene = deg,
  de_result_transcript = det,
  var = "condition",
  gene_name = "RBPJ"
)
head(profile)
plot_tx_expr(profile, gene_name = "RBPJ", group = "condition")
```

## Exon structures

`prepare_exon_annotation()` extracts the exon table of a set of genes from a GFF3 or GTF file for `plot_genomic_context()`; here from the small GFF3 bundled with the package.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 7
gff <- fs::path(extdata, "example.gff3")
exons <- prepare_exon_annotation("RBPJ", gff, output_path = tempdir())
head(exons)
plot_genomic_context(exons, gene_name = "RBPJ")
```

## Structural features and enrichment

`transcript_features()`, `transcript_orfs()`, `transcript_productivity()` and `polya_sites()` accept an annotation directory in place of the object, and `run_enrichment()` accepts a transcript table together with a `tx_to_gene` table.

```{r}
feats <- transcript_features(annot_dir, gene_name = "RBPJ")
feats[, c("transcript_name", "orf_length", "utr3_length", "nmd_predicted", "tss_group")]
```
